hypothesis: A containerized microservice architecture with a dedicated feature service, async queue-based ingress, and auto-scaled GPU model-serving pods ("treatment") can provide materially better end-to-end latency predictability, error isolation, and operational observability for watermark removal detection at platform scale than a simpler monolithic API deployment with in-process preprocessing and model inference ("baseline"), under comparable workloads and hardware budgets.

baseline.description: Monolithic detection API service with in-process preprocessing and model inference, directly exposed to clients.

components: Single containerized web API (e.g., FastAPI/uvicorn) exposing `/detect` endpoint over HTTP/JSON.
In-process image preprocessing (decode, resize, normalization) implemented in Python.
In-process model inference using a pre-loaded image watermark-removal detector (CPU or single GPU).
Synchronous writes from the API to a relational database (e.g., PostgreSQL) for logging and audit events.
Simple service-level metrics via application logging and a basic Prometheus exporter embedded in the API.
No separate feature store or feature service; features are computed ad hoc per request.

deployment.orchestration: docker-compose with a single replica of the API service plus a PostgreSQL container and a Prometheus container.
deployment.networking: Client requests -> Nginx reverse proxy (optional) -> API container.
deployment.scaling: Vertical scaling only (more CPU/GPU per container); no horizontal auto-scaling.

data_flow.ingress: Client sends image (binary or base64) and metadata directly to `/detect`.
data_flow.processing: API decodes image, applies preprocessing, performs model inference.
data_flow.decision: API returns detection score and label synchronously within the same HTTP response.
data_flow.logging: API writes raw request metadata, model scores, and decision to PostgreSQL in the synchronous request path.
data_flow.audit: Audit queries read from PostgreSQL; no separate audit event stream.

treatment.description: Modular microservice architecture separating ingestion, feature extraction, model serving, and logging/audit, deployed as containerized services backed by a message queue and auto-scaled GPU inference workers.

components: Ingress Gateway Service (`ingress-gw`): lightweight HTTP/JSON API for `/detect` and `/health`, responsible only for authentication, basic validation, and enqueueing detection jobs.
Detection Queue (`detect-queue`): durable message broker (e.g., Redis Streams or RabbitMQ) buffering detection jobs between ingress and workers.

Preprocessing & Feature Service (`feature-svc`): stateless workers consuming from `detect-queue`, performing image decode, normalization, and optional forensic feature extraction, then writing feature vectors and metadata to an online feature store.

Model Serving Service (`model-svc`): GPU-accelerated microservice exposing a gRPC/HTTP inference endpoint, consuming either raw images from `detect-queue` or precomputed features from `feature-svc`/feature store, returning scores and labels.

Aggregation & Response Service (`aggregator-svc`): correlates ingress requests with detection outputs (from `model-svc` via internal queue or callback), applies business logic (thresholds, policies) and returns responses to clients via callback or polling API.

Moderation Integration Service (`moderation-sink`): subscribes to detection decisions and pushes structured events into a simulated moderation system (e.g., Kafka topic or dedicated PostgreSQL schema) for downstream review tools.

Logging & Audit Service (`audit-log-svc`): independent write-only service receiving append-only detection and decision logs (via HTTP/gRPC or Kafka) and persisting them to PostgreSQL, minimizing coupling between online path and audit storage.
Observability Stack: Prometheus + Grafana containers collecting metrics from all services; structured JSON logging shipped to a local log aggregator (e.g., Loki or file-based sink).

deployment.containerization: Separate Docker images for each service: `ingress-gw`, `feature-svc`, `model-svc`, `aggregator-svc`, `moderation-sink`, `audit-log-svc`, `queue-broker`, `postgres`, `prometheus`, `grafana`.
deployment.orchestration: docker-compose-based reference deployment with configurable replica counts for `feature-svc` and `model-svc` to emulate horizontal scaling; optional Kubernetes manifests for cluster environments.
deployment.networking: Client -> `ingress-gw` (HTTP) -> `detect-queue`; internal services communicate via queues and internal service mesh (compose network). `model-svc` exposes gRPC/HTTP to `feature-svc`/`aggregator-svc` only.
deployment.scaling: Horizontal scaling knobs on `model-svc` and `feature-svc` (multiple replicas) with synthetic auto-scaling policies (triggered in experiments by queue depth or CPU/GPU utilization).

real_time_path: Client issues `/detect` request to `ingress-gw` with image reference or payload.
`ingress-gw` enqueues job into `detect-queue` and returns a correlation ID.
`feature-svc` consumes jobs, performs preprocessing/feature extraction, and forwards a model-ready payload to `model-svc` (sync) or a `model-input` queue (async).
`model-svc` runs detector inference on GPU and publishes results to a `results` stream.
`aggregator-svc` consumes from `results`, applies thresholding/policy logic, and emits structured decision events to both `moderation-sink` and `audit-log-svc`.
Client retrieves final decision via `GET /detect/{correlation_id}` or via a callback webhook (simulated in experiments).
batch_path: Batch job generator enqueues detection tasks for a directory or manifest of images.
Same internal pipeline as above, but latency SLOs are relaxed and throughput/efficiency metrics emphasized.

workloads.name: wl1-real-time-low-rps
workloads.description: Low throughput, latency-sensitive real-time detection workload emulating a smaller platform or early-stage rollout.

workloads.name: wl2-real-time-bursty-high-rps
workloads.description: High-throughput, bursty real-time workload approximating peak upload times on a large platform.

workloads.name: wl3-batch-backfill
workloads.description: Batch processing workload representing backfill re-scoring of an historical content corpus.

workloads.name: wl4-failure-injection
workloads.description: Resilience and safe-rollout workload with induced faults (model crash, DB slowness, queue partition) to observe fallback behavior and availability.

model_artifacts.detector_image_model: Pinned version of image watermark removal detector from `experiments/ch6_image_models/artifacts/model_v1.pt`.
model_artifacts.preprocessing_config: Shared preprocessing parameters (resize, normalization) defined in `configs/preprocessing/default.yaml`.

hardware.host_machine: Single physical host or reserved VM with identical specifications for baseline and treatment runs.
hardware.gpu: 1x NVIDIA GPU with >= 8 GB VRAM (e.g., T4 or equivalent); both baseline and treatment `model-svc` use this GPU.
hardware.storage: 500 GB SSD for logs, database, and container images.

software_stack.orchestration: docker-compose (>= 2.x) for the reference experiment; optional Kubernetes manifests are out-of-scope for core metrics but may be explored by readers.
software_stack.dl_framework: Pinned PyTorch/TensorFlow version consistent with earlier modeling chapters.
software_stack.infra_tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Redis or RabbitMQ, Nginx (optional).

dataset.source: Common evaluation dataset constructed in Chapter 4 and used in Chapters 5–10.
dataset.split: Fixed evaluation manifest (list of image paths and labels) stored under `data/manifests/ch11_system_eval.jsonl`.
dataset.assignment: All workloads draw from the same manifest with randomized but reproducible sampling via fixed seeds.

measurement.metrics_collection: All latencies, error codes, and queue metrics are recorded via Prometheus; audit correctness and moderation integration events are captured via PostgreSQL and structured logs.
measurement.time_synchronization: NTP-synchronized system clock across all containers; experiment scripts capture start and end times in UTC.
measurement.load_generation: Same load generator tool and configuration templates for baseline and treatment, only target endpoints differ.

metrics.name: p95_end_to_end_latency
metrics.description: 95th percentile latency from client request to final detection decision available to the client.

metrics.name: p99_end_to_end_latency
metrics.description: 99th percentile end-to-end latency from client request to detection decision.

metrics.name: mean_throughput
metrics.description: Average successfully processed detection requests per second over the workload duration.

metrics.name: error_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of requests resulting in 5xx or explicit application-level failure codes.

metrics.name: availability
metrics.description: Proportion of time during which the detection service meets a specified success criterion (e.g., non-error response within SLA).

metrics.name: queue_depth_peak
metrics.description: Maximum observed depth of detection job queue during workload.

metrics.name: cpu_utilization_model_service
metrics.description: Average CPU utilization for the model-serving component over workload.

metrics.name: gpu_utilization_model_service
metrics.description: Average GPU utilization for the model-serving component over workload.

metrics.name: moderation_event_delivery_latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile latency from model decision to moderation system receiving a structured event.

metrics.name: audit_log_write_success_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of detection decisions that are successfully persisted to the audit log store within a predefined time window.

metrics.name: sla_breach_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of requests whose end-to-end latency exceeds the defined SLA threshold (e.g., 500 ms real-time).

metrics.name: fallback_invocation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of requests for which a fallback path was used (e.g., cached score, degraded model, or default decision) due to model or infrastructure failures.

metrics.name: deployment_rollback_frequency
metrics.description: Number of rollbacks triggered during canary/shadow rollout scenarios in the experiment.

metrics.name: resource_cost_proxy
metrics.description: Approximate resource usage proxy combining CPU, memory, and GPU-time for all services during workload (e.g., CPU-core-seconds + GPU-memory-seconds).

metrics.name: observability_coverage_score
metrics.description: Qualitative or semi-quantitative score reflecting presence of key observability signals (per-request traces, high-cardinality labels, SLO error budget burn rates) mapped into a numeric scale for comparison.

primary.interpretation: Under peak/bursty load, the microservice-based treatment should yield at least 10% lower p95 latency than the monolith, indicating better latency predictability and headroom.
The treatment architecture should cut the rate of SLA breaches by at least half under high-RPS bursts.
During injected failures, overall availability (serving non-error responses within SLA) should improve by at least 2 percentage points in the treatment, due to better isolation and fallback.

secondary.interpretation: Moderation integration should not be slower in treatment; equal or better performance is expected.
Audit logging reliability must be at least 99% in treatment even under high load and fault injections.
Any improvements in latency and availability should not require more than a 25% increase in the approximate resource usage proxy.
The treatment architecture should materially improve observability coverage, reflecting richer metrics, traces, and SLO views.

qualitative: Treatment architecture demonstrates clear separation of responsibilities for real-time vs batch detection paths in reference deployment docs.
Safe rollout strategies (canary, shadow, fallback) are exercised and observable in the failure-injection workload without producing silent data loss in audit logs or moderation events.

failure_modes.name: measurement_artifacts
failure_modes.description: Differences in container placement, noisy neighbors, or host-level contention skew latency and throughput metrics between baseline and treatment.
mitigations: Run each experiment at least 3 times and report distributions, not single-run results.
Pin containers to dedicated host resources where possible; avoid concurrent unrelated workloads.
Monitor host-level CPU, memory, and disk I/O during experiments to rule out external interference.

failure_modes.name: non_comparable_configurations
failure_modes.description: Baseline and treatment use inconsistent model configurations or thresholds, causing differences in compute load and latency unrelated to architecture.
mitigations: Use identical model binaries and configuration files for both deployments.
Automate deployment configuration from shared YAML/JSON files and verify checksums before runs.

failure_modes.name: queue_backpressure_unbounded
failure_modes.description: In the treatment, the queue grows unbounded under bursty workloads, causing timeouts and skewed latency metrics.
mitigations: Configure maximum queue depth and rejection/backoff policies.
Monitor queue depth and include it in the analysis to distinguish queuing delays from processing inefficiencies.

failure_modes.name: audit_or_moderation_path_silent_failures
failure_modes.description: Decisions are served to clients but not logged or forwarded to moderation due to misconfigured sinks.
mitigations: Include integrity checks comparing counts of served responses vs audit records and moderation events.
Use transaction-like correlation IDs and consistency checks in analysis scripts.

failure_modes.name: improper_fault_injection
failure_modes.description: Failure injection in wl4 is too severe or too mild, making architectures appear equally bad or good.
mitigations: Pilot runs to calibrate fault intensity (e.g., partial degradation vs total outage).
Document injected fault parameters and ensure they are identical between baseline and treatment where applicable.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_specific_hardware
failure_modes.description: Observed benefits rely on specific GPU/CPU ratios or memory layouts that may not generalize.
mitigations: Repeat a subset of experiments on at least two hardware profiles (e.g., different GPU models) when feasible.
Document resource utilization patterns alongside latency/throughput metrics.

failure_modes.name: configuration_drift_between_runs
failure_modes.description: Changes in environment variables, dependencies, or container images between baseline and treatment runs invalidate comparability.
mitigations: Use immutable version tags for all containers and configuration bundles.
Capture a manifest of container image digests and environment settings with each experiment run.

os_and_runtime.os: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or compatible Linux distribution

security_and_governance.data_location: Use synthetic or pre-cleared evaluation datasets; no live user content.
security_and_governance.access_control: Local experiments do not require external network access beyond pulling container images; restrict DB and queue ports to localhost.
security_and_governance.logging: Ensure detection logs do not contain sensitive PII beyond synthetic identifiers in the reference setup.

preparation: Create and activate a Python virtual environment (optional but recommended).
Pull required Docker images: `docker compose -f deploy/ch11_system_architecture/baseline/compose.yaml pull` and similarly for `treatment/compose.yaml`.
Download or generate the shared evaluation dataset following Chapter 4 instructions; confirm that `data/manifests/ch11_system_eval.jsonl` exists.
baseline_run: Start the baseline stack: `docker compose -f deploy/ch11_system_architecture/baseline/compose.yaml up -d`.
Wait for services to become healthy (check with `docker compose ps` or health endpoints).
Run the load generator for each workload, pointing to the baseline endpoint (e.g., `BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080`):
For wl4 failure injection, start the fault injector in a separate terminal:

- Then run: `python experiments/ch11_system_architecture/loadgen/run_load.py --workload wl4-failure-injection --target-url http://localhost:8080/detect --manifest data/manifests/ch11_system_eval.jsonl --output-dir results/ch11/baseline/wl4/`
After all workloads finish, stop the baseline stack: `docker compose -f deploy/ch11_system_architecture/baseline/compose.yaml down`.
treatment_run: Start the treatment stack: `docker compose -f deploy/ch11_system_architecture/treatment/compose.yaml up -d`.
Confirm that gateway, queue, feature, model, aggregator, audit, moderation, DB, and observability services are healthy.
Run the load generator for each workload, targeting the treatment ingress endpoint, but using the same manifest and seeds:
For wl4, start the treatment-specific fault injector profile:

- Then run: `python experiments/ch11_system_architecture/loadgen/run_load.py --workload wl4-failure-injection --target-url http://localhost:9090/detect --manifest data/manifests/ch11_system_eval.jsonl --output-dir results/ch11/treatment/wl4/ --seed 1337`
After workloads complete, stop the treatment stack: `docker compose -f deploy/ch11_system_architecture/treatment/compose.yaml down`.
metrics_extraction_and_analysis: For each run, export Prometheus metrics to CSV or JSON using the metrics collector:

- `python experiments/ch11_system_architecture/metrics_collector/export_metrics.py --prometheus-url http://localhost:9091 --start-time <start> --end-time <end> --output results/ch11/baseline/wl2/metrics.json` (adapt paths and URLs as needed).
Run the analysis script to compute metrics defined in this spec:
Review the generated summary report (e.g., `results/ch11/summary/summary.json` and optional plots) to compare baseline vs treatment against success criteria.

Optional: Use Grafana dashboards defined under `deploy/ch11_system_architecture/observability/grafana_dashboards/` to visually inspect latency distributions, queue depth, and failure behaviors during runs.
reproducibility_notes: Ensure all commands are run with the same git commit checked out; record the commit hash in the summary report.
Avoid running other heavy workloads on the same machine during experiments.
If repeating experiments on different hardware, tag runs appropriately in the analysis script via `--label` flags.

fault_profile.description: Faults applied during this run, if any.

comparisons.description: Paired comparisons between baseline and treatment for each workload.

aggregated_metrics.description: Summary statistics per deployment type (e.g., mean and std across runs).

Relative paths to exported Grafana dashboard snapshots or images.
